text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Tuesday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Lithuanian and Latvian security department officials busted three Lithuanians suspected of smuggling drugs from Holland under the guise of a tourist company.

- The four tonnes of berrilium discovered in the basement of Innovation bank in 1993 was removed from the bank's premises on Monday. The prosecutor general declined to name where the material, used in nuclear warheads, was transferred.
- Lithuania's Savings Bank said it had a 226,000 litas net profit in April and a 1.957 million profit since the beginning of the year.
- Medicine Bank reported a 100,000 litas net profit in April and 337,000 litas profit in the first four months of 1997.
- The Centre Union Party has not decided who will be the party's candidate during December's presidential elections.
- Lithuania's Social Democrats intend to name their presidential candidate in June or September during the party's congress.
- Lithuania's privatisation agency failed to sell an 87 percent stake in the hotel Naujasis Vilnius since none of the potential buyers wanted to pay 15.7 million litas.
- People disabled on the job staged a rally in front of parliament and the government houses on Monday demanding higher compensation rates.
